after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Calculate the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\text{u}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]$ and $\text{v}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ \frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 \\ \frac{1}{3} & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{2}-6\cdot \frac{1}{3} \\  & =2-2 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|\,0\,|=0
$$

after.problem: Calculate the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\text{u}=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $\text{v}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 2 \\ 1 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2} & 2 \\ 1 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}| \\  & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}-2\cdot 1 \\  & =2-2 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The absolute value of $det(M)$ gives the area $A$ of the parallelogram:

$$
A=|\,0\,|=0
$$
